title: Leek and Potato Pie
subtitle: A creamy British shortcrust pie of soft leeks and floury potato
excerpt: Softened leeks and potato in a light cream sauce, baked inside a golden shortcrust shell. Simple, satisfying and good enough to stand as a main course.
sourceNotes: Classic British vegetable pie tradition, adapted from farmhouse baking practice for a standard 23cm pie dish.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze unbaked or baked. Reheat baked pie from frozen at 180C until hot through.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Assemble the pie a day ahead and refrigerate. Bake straight from the fridge, adding five minutes to the time.

content.text: This pie needs gentle cooking and patience. The leeks must be fully soft before they go in. A sauce that is too thin will give a soggy base, so cook it down until it just coats the back of a spoon.

items.prepNote: two thirds for the base, one third for the lid
cleaned, trimmed and sliced into 2cm rounds

content.text: Boil the potato cubes in salted water for 10 minutes until just tender. Drain and set aside.
Melt the butter in a wide pan over a low heat. Add the leeks and a pinch of salt. Cook gently for 12 minutes, stirring now and then, until completely soft.
Stir the flour into the leeks and cook for two minutes. Gradually pour in the milk, stirring all the time, until the sauce is smooth and thick enough to coat a spoon.
Stir in the potato and cheddar. Season well. Spread onto a plate and leave to cool completely before filling the pie.
Heat the oven to 200C. Line the pie dish with two thirds of the pastry, leaving a short overhang.
Spoon in the filling. Roll the rest of the pastry into a lid. Brush the rim with beaten egg and lay the lid on. Press firmly to seal, then trim the edge.
Cut two slits in the top and brush all over with egg. Bake for 40 to 45 minutes until deep golden. Rest for 10 minutes before slicing.

items.symptom: The filling is watery inside the pie.
items.cause: The sauce was too thin before it went in, or the leeks were not cooked long enough.
items.fix: Cook the sauce until a wooden spoon leaves a clear track. Undercooked leeks release water during baking.

items.symptom: The pastry base is pale and doughy.
items.cause: The pie dish sat on a cool shelf in the oven.
items.fix: Preheat a heavy baking tray and bake the pie on it. The direct heat firms the base quickly.

items.symptom: The lid pulls away from the sides.
items.cause: The egg wash was not brushed right to the edge before sealing.
items.fix: Brush all the way to the cut edge before pressing the lid down. Press firmly with a fork.
